gbm_population_evidence.quote: New Diagnosed with histologically or molecularly confirmed IDH wildtype and MGMT methylated GBM.

candidate_evidence.quote: MT-125 is a potent, selective, and central nervous system (CNS) permeable dual small molecule inhibitor of the non-muscle myosin II (NMII) paralogs, IIA and IIB.
This is an investigational new drug under IND 170975.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: New Diagnosed with histologically or molecularly confirmed IDH wildtype and MGMT methylated GBM.

tumour_pk_planned_evidence.quote: Area under the plasma concentration-time curve over the last 24 hour dosing interval.

role_evidence.quote: Here we will evaluate MT-125 as a monotherapy in a Phase 1/2 trial (NOVA-GBM) in newly diagnosed IDH wildtype / MGMT methylated GBM with standard of care RT and TMZ, following the standard chemoradiation treatment regimen.

agents.drug_class_hint: investigational small-molecule dual non-muscle myosin IIA/IIB inhibitor (MT-125)
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: dual inhibition of non-muscle myosin II paralogs IIA and IIB, interfering with tumour cell proliferation and invasion and generating reactive oxygen species
arms: MT-125 at MTD and one dose lower than MTD

role_evidence.quote: Up to 6 participants will receive 25 mg of MT-125 for 5 days then off for 2 days for a total of 6 weeks in combination of RT plus TMZ
The current well-known standard of care for newly diagnosed GBM is maximal safe surgical resection followed by concurrent RT with temozolomide (TMZ).

coder_notes: Temozolomide is not a registered intervention but every arm receives RT plus TMZ (standard chemoradiation), so listed as soc_backbone. Randomised expansion compares two MT-125 dose levels; no control arm. Only plasma PK planned. MGMT methylation required (linked to TMZ backbone, not candidate-matched).
